about: Test vectors for the X-Caddie-Admin v2 request signature (scripts/lib/admin-sign.mjs), which binds a signed admin request to the origin it is sent to, so a request that reaches another host cannot be replayed to the Worker. Generated by test/fixtures/admin-sign.v2.gen.mjs, never edited by hand: npm test fails when this file and the generator disagree. Everything test/fixtures/admin-sign.v1.json says holds for v2 unless stated here: the keys (UTF-8 after trimming, never hex-decoded, at least 32 characters), the path and query charsets, the body hash and the bodyless methods, the clock (`now` is Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000); all times are Unix seconds), and the order of the checks. Header: "v2 <ts> <nonce> <bodySha256> <sig>", single spaces, matching header_re: the v1 field grammar with "v2" in front (ts has no leading zero, nonce is 22 base64url characters, bodySha256 and sig are lowercase hex). Canonical string, UTF-8, exactly seven lines, each followed by one "\n" (LF, so the string ends with "\n"; no other separator, no "\r"): line 1 "caddie-admin-v2"; line 2 the method in upper case; line 3 new URL(path, base).pathname + search; line 4 bodySha256 as in the header; line 5 ts as in the header; line 6 nonce; line 7 the origin. That is canonical_format. sig is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of it. v1 has the same layout with "caddie-admin-v1" on line 1 and no line 7, so no v1 string equals a v2 string. The origin is not in the header. The client signs the origin of its base; the verifier holds a list of expected origins, normalises each the same way, drops duplicates and tries every (key, origin) pair, running every comparison. A signature made for an origin outside the list fails as "signature", with no reason of its own (Worker: 404). Origin values are read strictly by both sides (origin_rule, the "origin" cases): after trimming, printable ASCII only, a literal http:// or https:// prefix in any case, no "@", backslash, "%" or ",", the whole value matching origin_allow_re (a scheme, "//", a host of letters, digits, "." and "-" or a bracketed IPv6 address, an optional port, an optional final "/"), then new URL(x) must be an http: or https: URL with path "/" or none and no query, fragment, user name or password, and the value is new URL(x).origin (lowercase scheme and host, the default port dropped). An internationalised host is written in its punycode form; its Unicode form is refused. On the Worker (worker_admin_origin, worker_admin_sig_min): ADMIN_ORIGIN, when set, is the comma list of expected origins; when it is unset, or empty after trimming, the expected origin is new URL(request.url).origin. ADMIN_SIG_MIN is matched exactly. Only a set ADMIN_ORIGIN with a refused entry, or an ADMIN_SIG_MIN other than unset, "1" or "2", is invalid configuration, which answers 404 to every admin request, v1 included, with no failed-auth charge. worker_config_cases give the expected reading of raw ADMIN_ORIGIN and ADMIN_SIG_MIN values (raw absent means unset): parseAdminOrigin and parseAdminSigMin in scripts/lib/admin-origin.mjs, which has no imports, are the reference implementation. Four kinds of case. "sign": signer input with version 2 and the exact origin, canonical string and header it must produce; same_header_as names a case whose header must be identical. "verify": what the verifier answers for a header given the keys it holds, its allowed_versions, its expected_origins (absent means none were given) and its clock; expect.version is the header's version, expect.origin the expected origin that matched (v2 only), and expect.compares the number of constant-time comparisons made (no early exit). "reject": input refused before anything is sent or checked; call "sign" is signAdminRequest(input), call "verify" is verifyAdminSignature() refusing its own settings whatever the header. A reject case with node_api_only true has no Worker equivalent (see its note); the others are a set ADMIN_ORIGIN holding a refused entry. "origin": the normalisation of one value; origin null means refused.
origin_rule: x is a string; t = x.trim() (String.prototype.trim); t matches ^[\x21-\x7e]+$ (printable ASCII) and ^https?:// (case-insensitive), holds no "@", "\", "%" or "," (origin_forbidden_re), and matches origin_allow_re (case-insensitive; it implies the three checks before it); new URL(t) has protocol http: or https:, pathname "/", and empty search, hash, username and password; its hostname is the typed host in lower case and its port the typed port with the default port of the scheme (or an empty port) dropped, so a host the parser rewrites (a numeric IPv4 form other than a canonical dotted quad, an IPv6 address not in its canonical compressed form, a port with a leading zero) is refused; the result is new URL(t).origin. Anything else is refused.
worker_admin_origin: ADMIN_ORIGIN set (non-empty after trimming): split on ",", apply origin_rule to each entry, drop duplicates (mode "list"); any refused entry, including the empty one a stray comma leaves, is invalid configuration (mode "invalid": 404 for every admin request, v1 included, no failed-auth charge). ADMIN_ORIGIN unset, or empty after trimming (mode "fallback"): the expected origins are [new URL(request.url).origin], computed without origin_rule. List only hostnames that route to this Worker, never another deployment's origin.
worker_admin_sig_min: ADMIN_SIG_MIN unset, or exactly "1": allowed_versions [1, 2]. Exactly "2": allowed_versions [2]. Any other value, the empty string, surrounding whitespace and "02" included, is invalid configuration (allowed_versions null: 404 for every admin request, no failed-auth charge). The match is exact because a loose reading would fail open at step d.

verify_reasons._note: The reference verifier first checks its own settings (see the reject cases with call "verify"), then the header in this order: malformed, bodyless_body_hash, no_key, signature, skew, and reports the first that applies. A verifier may check no_key before malformed (the Worker does). When several reasons apply, any one of those applying reasons is acceptable; all map to 404, except skew, which is 401 admin_skew and can only follow a valid signature.
verify_reasons.malformed: the header is absent, matches neither header_re nor v1_header_re, or is of a version not in allowed_versions (Worker: 404)
verify_reasons.bodyless_body_hash: GET, HEAD or DELETE with a bodySha256 other than empty_body_sha256 (Worker: 404)
verify_reasons.no_key: the verifier holds no usable key (Worker: 404)
verify_reasons.signature: no held key reproduces sig: for v1 over the v1 canonical string, for v2 over the v2 canonical string with any expected origin; a wrong origin is this reason (Worker: take() the failed-auth bucket, 404)
verify_reasons.skew: |now - ts| > skew_seconds, checked only after the signature matched (Worker: 401 admin_skew)

reject_reasons._note: Each reject case names the UsageError.code thrown: by signAdminRequest(input) for call "sign", by verifyAdminSignature() for call "verify". Together with admin-sign.v1.json these are all the codes the module has.
reject_reasons.version: sign: version is neither the number 1 nor the number 2; verify (Node API only): allowed_versions is not a non-empty list of the numbers 1 and 2
reject_reasons.expected_origins: verify: 2 is allowed and expected_origins is missing, not a list or empty (Node API only), or holds an entry origin_rule refuses (fail closed: one bad entry refuses the list; on the Worker, a set ADMIN_ORIGIN with such an entry)
reject_reasons.url: sign: the base is not a URL or not an origin (as in v1), and for v2 also a base that origin_rule refuses (not printable ASCII, no literal http:// or https://, an "@" or a backslash, another scheme, credentials) or that is not a string
